If you've never had tea from England, it is not like tea you get in the states. It's got a stronger more robust taste and it's dark. I didn't know what a base Stitch is but my wife told me it's when somebody makes something by hand they Stitch It Together by hand and then they can use a machine to come along and actually tidy it up when they're ready to finish.

So anyway, like I said I don't write reviews and this is probably too long but this is a very nice product handmade and beautiful highly recommended.

Carefully I peeled the paper off the decal then, using the pencil line as a guide, applied the decal to the wall from the bottom up and left to right, smoothing out bubbles and correcting wrinkles as I went. Next I peeled off the backing paper very slowly, inch-by-inch as my little boy peppered me with queations about why I was going so slow, how long would the sticker last, and did I need any help.
? At last it was done and he was super happy. I'm hopeful it stays on the wall at least as long as his interest in Minecraft last.

I contacted Hannah and she told me to use the cleaning cloth provided and it should wipe away the black smudges. It did not. text:
These pretty earrings are super simple, very lightweight and a bit wide and long. The metal is about the width of a large paperclip and folded into a distinct heart shape that closes on the bottom, so these are worn either upside down or on the side. The closure depends on not pulling the metal back through the tiny hole as there's no lock or security, but should be fine if you don't play with them a lot or get the end caught on something. With normal wear, they're fine and I love the fact that they can look different at different angles and distances. Nothing overwhelming, just simple, pretty jewelry for those that don't like tiny pieces. Note: If you have a very short neck or wear thick clothes around your neck, the closure might get caught on the fabric.
I do recommend care as I think they will bend easily if abused. The company really should have put a tiny smooth round dot at the end so you don't poke yourself or get caught up in anything that gets too close.
But I like them anyway.
They come in a nice gift box with a cloth for cleaning (I guess) and is ready for gift giving. See the photos -- also, the pen next to the earrings is to show approximate length.

text: I purchased these earrings and presented them to a very dear friend of mine for a retirement gift.  My friend's favorite color is Turquoise/Sky Blue.  She was very clear that her retirement party theme was to include Turquoise/Sky Blue colors.  I came across these earrings and felt they would be a perfect gift for her as well as tie into the color theme of her retirement party.  I didn't know anything about "Sea Glass" when I made this purchase.  After making the purchase I decided to do a little research on "Sea Glass".  What I found was that the "Sea Glass" used to create these earrings was mechanically processed to resemble sea glass and not true/authentic "Sea Glass".  True/authentic "Sea Glass" is glass that has been discarded into the sea/ocean, broken into pieces, and smoothed by the erosive action of sand and water over years.  I felt somewhat "cheated" by the fact that I thought I was purchasing "real" "Sea Glass".  But I've learned a lesson.  On another note, the earrings are beautiful and the price wasn't too bad.  Real "Sea Glass", depending on the quality, can vary greatly in price.

text:
These removable wallpaper stickers were simple to apply. It takes time and patience, but it is not difficult!

After painting the bathroom walls (not textured) black, and allowing the paint to dry for a few days, I cut around every sticker, allowing about an inch beyond each design. Next, with the help of a friend, I held each one up to get an idea of where I wanted each, and layed out a design on the bedroom floor. Once I decided my layout, it was time to begin.

I started in the middle, at the height of my design, and one by one placed each sticker up. The pre-cut detailed edges of each flower can easily fold, and stick to other parts of itself, so be careful to hold up as you peel off backing to avoid a mishap like this. Begin adhering to the wall in the center, and push out toward the edges, pressing air bubbles out. I used my palm of my hand, washed of course. No special tool was needed.

This process was used for each individual flower sticker, taking care to overlap flowers so the arrangement looked natural. The stickers adhere so well, that it wasn’t easy to lift the already adhered sticker in order to layer/overlap. I used a stainless steel drywall tool to lift the delicate edges. This tool is used to apply and flatten spackle/mud (I don’t know the name of the tool), and its edge is thin, like a knife. It has a handle and a 5 inch “paddle.” Imagine a ping pong paddle, but very thin steel, in a rectangular shape. I tried a plastic version of this tool, but the steel one worked much better. This tool saved the integrity of the delicate edges. Just using a fingernail tended to bend the stickers edges, making it difficult to reapply smoothly. In the case of overlapping a large area of a flower, I did trim excess with a scissor.

I’m pleasantly surprised to see that, once applied, the overlaps are not visible.

I had a friend, who knows that I myself paint, come over; and he actually got very close, and ran his hand over the wall, while asking, did you paint all this?! The finished design is absolutely beautiful! I’m very picky, and I do not have the urge to take them down and paint a design myself, LOL!

I do wish I could purchase the vinyl sticker pages, without a design printed, to paint myself, and make my own wallpaper stickers in the future!!!

text:
I bought 5 of these rings - one in each color. I have 5 children so it worked out perfectly! I've now worn the rings every single day for just about a year and wanted to review them. First of all, I still absolutely love them and they were exactly what I wanted. No green rings, no irritation, feel just as sturdy as my wedding band :)
The following issue don't bother me at all but are worth noting for other would-be-purchasers:
1) The black inside the writing comes off VERY quickly. Within a couple of days/hand washes/etc. it started coming out and so I ended up just scraping it out of all of them rather then having random parts missing.
2) The two silver ones (I think it was matte and shiny) - within maybe a month or so - they look the same (both shiny). This doesn't bother me because I wear the two silver on one hand and the three other colors on the other. Which brings me to
3) I bought the five hoping I could stack them all on one finger. Not so :( in fairness, I'm generally a petite person - but even 4 on one finger was a bit snug. If you want to stack them - it's most realistic to just assume 3 on one finger.
4) The gold colors also fade (again - in fairness, I've been wearing these rings EVERY day and never take them off for any reason!) but the chocolate one is still somewhat distinct but the other two have faded to looking somewhat close in color. Again, in fairness - my wedding band is a cartier trinity ring of white, yellow and rose gold and it also has completely faded bc I don't take care of it!

So - in conclusion - these rings were better then I even expected! I was looking for rings to represent my kids who are older and beginning to transition to their adult lives and I wanted to keep them with me like my husband on my hand :) and these are just perfect for it despite the reality of daily wear!

text: I read many, many reviews to try and glean some sort of best process to do this for those that had success with these.  I finally got time to get mine on the wall (and they look fantastic, I'm so happy with the end result) and this is what worked for me: flattening the large roll of paper that the stickers come on, cutting out the shapes and hanging up with painters tape before applying, take pictures once you have your preferred pattern (painters tape only holds for so long), have a buddy helping out to keep you sane.  Each person will have their own idea for layout, but if you want clusters like I did (in pic), really think about what needs to go down first because while you can lift and replace on the wall ok, maybe once or twice, the stickers stick REALLY WELL to each other and are not as forgiving.  I put down leaves first and then went flowers, placing down any leaves that I had overlapping as needed.  It worked best for me to start a sticker and keep the back on and kind of roll that paper up as I set the sticker on the wall, especially the bigger flowers.  I also bought tools to help smooth them out and prevent air bubbles as I pressed them down, it helped so much.  One reviewer suggested to heat set with a hairdryer if you plan to have them up for a long time, I did that, seemed to help.  They've been up for about 2 weeks now with no problems, no hint of peeling up or falling off the wall.  This went in my smaller room that I use as a home office/guest bedroom and I used every sticker from the 2 sets that I ordered.  Took me about 6-8 hours total with help (slow and steady). text:
I have always admired bottle trees and thought it would be fun to add one to my garden. This 13 bottle tree is perfect!
It's really well made. As a matter of fact the directions say the bottles will break before the welds do. Excellent directions make for a super easy set up. The hardest part was pounding it into the ground. I was worried that the tree would not go far enough into the ground to be stable, especially with the extreme wind gusts we get, so I found a 2' section of iron pipe that the tree "trunk" fit into, and pounded the pipe into the ground first. Worked just fine.
The branches are all the same length, which made for a column shaped tree with regular 750ml wine bottles. A trip to the liquor store solved that problem. I found much larger, longer 2 l wine bottles that I used for the lowest branches, 1l bottles for the next 2 sets of branches, traditional 750 ml bottles for the next 2 sets of branches, fancy 500 ml water bottles for the top pair and a red 750 ml wine bottle for the single top. It's more pyramidal shaped like a conifer tree. I chose not to spray seal the metal, preferring for it to weather naturally.
Quite the whimsical conversation piece. And made by a small company in the USA! There are several sizes and shapes available. Highly recommend.

text:
The craftsmanship on this was wanting. The bar in the front that is designed to keep whatever you display from falling off is not flush with the unit. You can see from my photo that you can see daylight clear all the way through. It wiggles if you touch it. If only adults live in your house, it may never be an issue, but if you have kids at all I would hesitate before buying.

Also, I don't know whether it's the stain or if it's tree sap, but there's some material on this that is sticky as hell. You can see in the photo of my finger the discoloration that's still left after trying to wash that stuff off. It was only on the sides, so fortunately not anywhere that a coat I might hang would sit.

On the whole, I don't believe this comes close to justifying the price tag. This feels like someone at home said, "$100 for a wall coat rack? I can do that!" Then they didn't actually bother to learn real wood working and slapped this together. It truly does feel like 3 boards of wood with 8 hooks screwed onto it. In this particular instance, very truly, I could have done *that* and it would have simply cost me the hardware and about 20 minutes of work. For $120, I expect better.

text:
Update July 2021: These are still stunning, have never faded, have not peeled or rolled and are still on the wall as I originally placed them- even with it getting humid and hot at times. We get compliments on them all the time and I'm very happy with how it all turned out. I felt like I wanted to know this when I was considering buying and reading reviews so I hope this update helps someone!

Original post March 2021: I bought two rolls of the flowers for our daughter's nursery and since the ceilings are high and vaulted, I wasn't sure if one would've been sufficient for the kind of coverage I was looking for (also wanted to give myself room for error, based on some of the reviews on here.) Didn't need them immediately and wanted to follow the advice of another customer who'd suggested laying them flat for a while before hanging, so I did. In fact, I ended up leaving them flat for at least a month (probably overkill but I was preoccupied with other baby-related tasks, so it didn't bother me.) I'd say if you're able, leave them flat somewhere in the room where you plan to hang them for at least two weeks, to be safe.

*To answer the million-dollar question (did they adhere or did they roll up a day after?):

-They did adhere, really really well actually. Be sure you're committed to your layout before taking the backing off. It's not impossible to take one off right after placing if you have to move it, but you have to be patient and gentle to avoid messing it up or having it stick to itself.

-The day after we hung them, I did notice that I had to use a finger to smooth down an edge here or there, but they'd only lifted about 2mm or so and since then I haven't had any issues with them threatening to roll off of the wall. Again, I think keeping them flat in the room where they were to hang helped a lot, as they weren't moving to a space with different temperature, humidity, etc. which could've made getting good adherence difficult.

-Also, I did not clean nor prep the wall. I did not paint and then try to hang a week later... Our walls are a standard, smooth texture. If our palms started to sweat even a little, we used a hand towel to dry them off before resuming with hanging again to prevent moisture getting onto the backing. Take your time and be sensible.

- It's been a week now without any lifting etc., so I'm feeling confident that these are going to stay put.

*Application:

-I used our ladder and hung them on the wall first with blue painters tape so I could play around with design (HIGHLY RECOMMEND THIS,) and then my husband and father-in-law placed them from there. They made sure to keep a hand on each applique and slowly remove the backing in a top-to-bottom fashion, and used their hands plus a small squeegee-like item to push out and prevent air bubbles (squeegee doesn't need to be anything special. We used a small tool that's square with beveled edges from pampered chef. A light weight, hardcover book or something would probably work well.)

Once mounted, these flowers look almost as if they've been painted on. They're quite stunning in person and I can't stop looking at them! Finally, an "Insta-worthy" end product that I actually put together. Hopefully you'll be patting yourself on the back once it's all said and done as well!

Side note: The custom name sign was purchased on Etsy. Look-up "TheWhimsyTimber" and you'll find them. Top notch business!!

I do not know if this was a new piecing or not as that wasn't specified by the reviewer. If your piercing is new & has not completely healed, never put in new jewelry, including sterling silver jewelry. Sterling silver will irritate new piercings that aren't fully healed, even if you *think* your new piercing is fully healed, it's best to wait at least 4 to 6 months. But again, I don't know if that was their actual issue so leave it to me to be the guinea pig. text:
This is exactly as advertised. If you want something quirky to give as a gift there are few better.

How could I have such a beautiful piece of art, however, without a story to go along with it before I gave it to my son? The following was written to go along with this item:

The story of the little Corgi that couldn’t – at least not without a sweet ride

Once upon a time there was a little corgi named Corgu…

Corgu was the runt of his litter. His bigger brothers and sisters were all strong and healthy and could take on a chew toy with the best of them. But not Corgu… Corgu would pounce on his chew toy only to have it roll over on top of him and subsequently pin him to the ground. He would have to yelp and make noises until one of his siblings could come over and help him remove it from on top of him.

It was humiliating...

While other Corgis could run after a ball and play fetch at the beach all he could do was run after the ball and do his best to push it with his nose because he wasn’t strong enough to lift the ball with his mouth and carry it back to his master.

Because he was a runt he found that other Corgis didn’t want to spend time with him. He did his best to find other friends but time after time he was shunned because he was so small – that is until one day he came across a nest of eggs and noticed that one of the eggs was smaller than the others. He would go every day to see how the eggs were doing and finally one day they all hatched. He had found a nest full of velociraptors and just like him, one of them was a runt. His name was Yoshi and they became the best of friends.

They were used to all of the others in their school class making fun of them. They knew they were tiny and together they spent time running around, and pretending they were big like the other animals in their class. They were resigned to the fact that they would pretty much be ignored.

Then one day it happened.

While they were on the playground an enormous T-rex crashed through the fence and started eating all of their classmates. While everyone else around them was screaming and running away Corgu and Yoshi knew that they would have to do something or there wouldn’t be anyone left… So Corgu ran to the woods on the edge of the playground and grabbed a stick while Yoshi ran into the school and grabbed a knife from the cafeteria. They quickly strapped the knife to the stick and Corgu jumped on top of Yoshi and together they charged the T-rex.

I wish I had good news to tell you about Corgu and Yoshi but as they approached the T-rex he opened his jaws and clamped down on them both. But after chewing his newest meal the spear they had created got stuck in his throat and tore him inside all the way down to his stomach and he died a horrible death.

The other animals stood amazed at the bravery and sacrifice that these two runts had made just for them and quickly drew a picture of the brave friends on the only piece of paper they could find – a page they tore from the dictionary in the school library.

Time passed as time does, and the school was closed and sat derelict for centuries. Until I stumbled upon it while I lived in Illinois in the woods back behind my high school. I found the picture clinging to one of the few remaining walls along with the story of the brave friends.

Son, I am passing this treasured find on to you to treasure and pass along to your posterity. Never forget the bravery of Corgu and Yoshi. May it always serve as a means of inspiring you to greater and greater things.

text: The modern design and size were perfect for our Florida home.  I was a little concerned with previous reviews showing many screws extended beyond the back when they wanted a flush mount.  Our vertical flush mount plaque only had two mounting screws extending beyond the back.  The others were flush to the nuts which caused about 1/16” gap between the stucco exterior and the back of the address plaque.  Installation was easy (about 30 mins) even though our home is constructed with cinder blocks; just use the correct type of drill-bit for your anchor holes.  I drilled the top hole first, inserted the top screw into the hole and then used a level to ensure the plaque was square before marking and drilling the bottom hole.  After drilling the holes, I inserted both mounting screws to ensure they were deep enough for flushing mounting and was still square.  Once satisfied, I applied G Glue to the screws and the nuts (even though the nuts are not mentioned in the instructions) for maximum adhesion for the Florida wind.  I was going to caulk the gap between the stucco exterior and the back of the plaque but decided it wasn’t necessary after I completed the installation.

text: We have purchased and worked with vinyl from other sellers before and usually there is a bit of a learning curve for getting the vinyl just right, but this vinyl was easy to work with and was up on the wall within 10 minutes!  We washed the wall, leveled and centered the name, using a pencil to mark the wall.  We pulled the back paper off just a few inches at a time, smoothing the vinyl to the wall as you go.  The included plastic smoother was perfect.  You don't want to go too quickly or you could mess up the little pieces of vinyl that stick out and/or the creeper face.  Once you have the entire sign on the wall and you're sure it's adhering to the wall, you gently peel back the front paper so that the vinyl is exposed.  We used a dry wash cloth to rub over it to help remove any bubbles, etc.  My Minecraft fan absolutely lives it.

The competitors pork puller that sells for $30 more has this feature and this one does not. It would be a big feature and to Don's benefit to incorporate this feature into his next new version. So Don' if you get a chance to read this review I would be willing to "Beta Test" your next new model and updated version of your product. text: I was surprised to see this has a 4.2 star rating when I came to reorder it for the third time. I love this nose ring, and the only reason I have had to reorder it is because of accidents where it got damaged (I have young kids who always find a way to headbutt me). I have tried plenty of other nose rings. They've either tarnished or caused irritation to my skin. This does not tarnish and never has given me a reaction. If you're having an issue getting it to stay in or to fit in your nostril without scratching you, the issue isn't the product, it's that you've not put it in correctly. You either need to have a piercer do it for you or you need jewelry pliers and need to practice lining up the two ends properly.
